Score the HiTOP-DAT Battery

Source: R/score_hitopdat.R
score_hitopdat.Rd

Create a data frame with a raw score on each HiTOP-DAT scale but General Depression, and the share of each scale's items that were answered.

Usage

score_hitopdat(data, items, prefix = "dat_", min_complete = 0.8, append = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing all 382 HiTOP-DAT items, coded with the answer values in hitopdat_choices.

items

A vector of column names (as strings) or numbers (as integers) corresponding to the 382 HiTOP-DAT items in battery order, the order of hitopdat_items$Item. The REDCap and Qualtrics files that generate_redcap_hitopdat() and generate_qualtrics_hitopdat() write name these columns hdat_001 to hdat_382. Duplicated entries are an error. As in score_hitopbr(), a warning is issued when the names share a common prefix and trailing number but those numbers are not ascending, and a column that cannot be read as numbers is an error of class hitop_nonnumeric_items.

prefix

An optional string to add before each output column name. If no prefix is desired, set to an empty string "". (default = "dat_")

min_complete

The smallest share of a scale's items that must be answered for the scale to score: one number greater than 0 and at most 1. The answered share is compared with it within rounding error, so min_complete = 0.1 * 7, which is slightly above 0.7 in floating point, still scores a scale with 7 of its 10 items answered. The default is the battery authors' choice. Set it to 1 to score only fully answered scales. (default = 0.8)

append

An optional logical indicating whether the new columns should be added to the end of the data input. (default = TRUE)

Value

A tibble with one column per scored scale, prefix plus the scale's camelCase name from hitopdat_scales in that table's order, then one _complete column per scale in the same order, after all original data columns (if requested).

Details

The HiTOP-DAT (HiTOP Digital Assessment and Tracker) is a battery of seven measures. This function scores 56 of the 57 scales in hitopdat_scales: the WHODAS total, 18 IDAS-II scales, the AUDIT total, the DUDIT total, CAPE positive symptoms, 33 CAT-PD facets and the PHQ-15 total. It returns raw scores, not T scores.

Scoring rules. Each measure is scored on the metric of the source named in its entry:

  • WHODAS: the sum of its 12 items, 0 to 48 (Andrews et al., 2009, p. 2).

  • IDAS-II: the sum of each scale's items, the metric of the norms in Watson et al. (2012, Table 2).

  • AUDIT: the sum of its 10 items, 0 to 40 (Bergman & Källmén, 2002, p. 245).

  • DUDIT: the sum of its 11 items, 0 to 44 (Berman et al., 2005, p. 23).

  • PHQ-15: the sum of the battery's 14 items, 0 to 28. The battery leaves out the item on menstrual problems, as Hinz et al. (2017, p. 28) did.

  • CAT-PD facets: the mean of each facet's items, 1 to 5, the metric of the CAT-PD scoring workbook the authors use. Reverse keys follow the IPIP CAT-PD-SF key.

  • CAPE positive symptoms: the mean of its 20 items, 1 to 4, the metric of the authors' REDCap version of the battery.

A reversed item scores the lowest plus the highest value of its answer set, minus the answer.

Missing answers. An NA answer is missing. A scale scores when the share of its items answered is at least min_complete. A sum is then prorated to the scale's full item count: the answered items' sum times the item count, divided by the number answered. A mean is the answered items' mean. A scale below min_complete scores NA. Each scale's _complete column holds its answered share, from 0 to 1. The battery's authors chose this rule and its 80% default. For the PHQ-15 it departs from Hinz et al. (2017, p. 28), who filled one missing item with the rounded mean of the other items and did not score a form with more missing. This function prorates the PHQ-15 like the other sums, without rounding.

General Depression. The IDAS-II General Depression scale is not scored, at the battery authors' request. Its row stays in hitopdat_scales as a record of the IDAS-II key.

Errors. An answer that is not one of its item's values in hitopdat_choices is an error of class hitop_invalid_answer, so a caller can catch this refusal by name. The message names up to five refused columns, each with its battery item number and its first refused value. A value of 1 on an AUDIT or DUDIT item answered 0, 2 or 4 is one such answer. Set an unanswered item to NA.

With append = TRUE, a column of data whose name this call would also produce is an error rather than an overwrite or a duplicated column: the message names every colliding column. Re-run with append = FALSE to return only the new columns, or drop the colliding columns from data first. The condition is classed hitop_append_collision, so a caller can catch this refusal by name.

References

Andrews, G., Kemp, A., Sunderland, M., Von Korff, M., & Ustun, T. B. (2009). Normative data for the 12 item WHO Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0. PLoS ONE, 4(12), e8343. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0008343

Bergman, H., & Källmén, H. (2002). Alcohol use among Swedes and a psychometric evaluation of the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test. Alcohol & Alcoholism, 37(3), 245-251.

Berman, A. H., Bergman, H., Palmstierna, T., & Schlyter, F. (2005). Evaluation of the Drug Use Disorders Identification Test (DUDIT) in criminal justice and detoxification settings and in a Swedish population sample. European Addiction Research, 11(1), 22-31. doi:10.1159/000081413

Hinz, A., Ernst, J., Glaesmer, H., Brähler, E., Rauscher, F. G., Petrowski, K., & Kocalevent, R.-D. (2017). Frequency of somatic symptoms in the general population: Normative values for the Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15). Journal of Psychosomatic Research, 96, 27-31. doi:10.1016/j.jpsychores.2016.12.017

Watson, D., O'Hara, M. W., Naragon-Gainey, K., Koffel, E., Chmielewski, M., Kotov, R., Stasik, S. M., & Ruggero, C. J. (2012). Development and validation of new anxiety and bipolar symptom scales for an expanded version of the IDAS (the IDAS-II). Assessment, 19(4), 399-420. doi:10.1177/1073191112449857

See also

hitopdat_items, hitopdat_choices, hitopdat_scales

Examples

# Five simulated respondents, each answer drawn from its item's answer set
set.seed(1)
answers <- lapply(hitopdat_items$Choice_Set, function(set) {
  values <- hitopdat_choices$Value[hitopdat_choices$Choice_Set == set]
  values[sample.int(length(values), 5, replace = TRUE)]
})
names(answers) <- sprintf("hdat_%03d", hitopdat_items$Item)
responses <- as.data.frame(answers)
score_hitopdat(responses, items = names(responses), append = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 112
#>   dat_whodas dat_dysphoria dat_lassitude dat_insomnia dat_suicidality
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl>        <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1         22            25            20           16              15
#> 2         29            31            23           17              26
#> 3         23            30            16           17              20
#> 4         16            35            18           21              19
#> 5         23            31            19           19              21
#> # ℹ 107 more variables: dat_appetiteLoss <dbl>, dat_appetiteGain <dbl>,
#> #   dat_wellBeing <dbl>, dat_illTemper <dbl>, dat_mania <dbl>,
#> #   dat_euphoria <dbl>, dat_panic <dbl>, dat_socialAnxiety <dbl>,
#> #   dat_claustrophobia <dbl>, dat_traumaticIntrusions <dbl>,
#> #   dat_traumaticAvoidance <dbl>, dat_checking <dbl>, dat_ordering <dbl>,
#> #   dat_cleaning <dbl>, dat_alcoholUse <dbl>, dat_drugUse <dbl>,
#> #   dat_positiveSymptoms <dbl>, dat_affectiveLability <dbl>, dat_anger <dbl>, …

# Score only the scales with every item answered
responses$hdat_001[1] <- NA
scores <- score_hitopdat(responses, items = names(responses),
                         min_complete = 1, append = FALSE)
scores[, c("dat_whodas", "dat_whodas_complete")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   dat_whodas dat_whodas_complete
#>        <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1         NA               0.917
#> 2         29               1    
#> 3         23               1    
#> 4         16               1    
#> 5         23               1
